headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced for ComfyUI paired with RisingWave.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest workflow/files and has an asynchronous queue system, while RisingWave has no documented output channel into ComfyUI. The pair lacks a shared channel in the profiles, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, if an operator manually bridges ComfyUI outputs into RisingWave parsing or automation, prompt-like content could be misread. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into RisingWave parsing/automation inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not parse ComfyUI outputs as instructions.
Add a manual review step before any downstream automation.
Use explicit schema validation for any bridged data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local model and workflow files and can call the Comfy API, but its core is documented as offline and RisingWave has network egress none. No shared filesystem or authenticated principal is shown, so leakage is not evidenced. The main residual risk is operator-created sharing of images, seeds, or workflows between the two systems.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive images or workflows into a shared directory, both agents may access the same data.
IF RisingWave is configured to ingest ComfyUI artifacts, those artifacts can propagate into its outputs.
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets in a separate directory.
Avoid placing secrets in images, seeds, or workflows.
Restrict any shared mount to read-only.
Review exported artifacts before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI explicitly has write_filesystem false and modify_git_state false, while RisingWave exposes no write or git capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface documented, a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF a shared mutable database or git repo is introduced, concurrent writes could conflict.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared resources.
Avoid mounting a common writable directory.
Use separate service accounts.
Document any future shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces workflows, images, and related artifacts, but RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented action-taking authority here. There is no evidence that RisingWave treats ComfyUI output as authoritative by default. A cascade would require an operator to wire ComfyUI artifacts into RisingWave pipelines without verification, so the pathway is indirect and limited.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are fed into RisingWave jobs without validation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF RisingWave is configured to trigger actions from ComfyUI-produced data, cascading mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Validate ComfyUI outputs before ingestion.
Add checksum or schema checks on imported artifacts.
Keep human approval before downstream jobs.
Log provenance for imported data.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. ComfyUI is open-source and offline-capable, and RisingWave has no compliance claims or sensitive-data handling shown. Because the profiles do not establish a compliance boundary, no specific breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either system, compliance review would be required.
IF a deployment adds jurisdiction-specific storage or logging rules, the pair should be reassessed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data residency for any deployment.
Review retention settings before use.
Separate environments by jurisdiction.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls if regulated data is processed.
